meta.note: Typed up from photos of the cards and recordings of each group reading aloud. Spelling and wording are as written, except that the team's shorthand for our name is written out in full. Groups D and E's cards weren't photographed, so their headlines come from the recordings. Two cards are partly cut off in the photos: one of group B's peer cards (the Aspen Institute) and one of group C's impact cards.

headlines.text: The Upskilling Labs is federated across every US community, driving a deep understanding and development of autonomy and agency in every personal digital interaction, keeping citizens relevant and equal participants in the workforce, and AI policy.
headlines.spoken: We have Upskilling Labs federated across every US community, driving a deep understanding and development of autonomy and agency in every personal digital interaction, keeping citizens relevant and equal participants in the workforce and AI policy. So, super wordy. The big one there: proliferating across the country.
headlines.future: autonomy and agency in every personal digital interaction; citizens relevant and equal participants in the workforce and AI policy

headlines.text: The Upskilling Labs working with 100+ local + national govts + 10,000,000 upskillers
headlines.spoken: Upskilling Labs working with a hundred local and national governments plus 10 million upskillers globally. Bigger stakeholders, but keeping true to our main focus: helping local communities and individuals grow their skills, grow their confidence and build community.
headlines.position: working with 100+ local and national governments and 10 million upskillers

headlines.text: Every community that hosts an Upskilling Labs attracts private + public investment. Every member of that community is gainfully employed in a fulfilling role. Communities have what they need to solve problems for public & private sectors at the local, national & global levels.
headlines.spoken: Two statements. Every community that hosts an Upskilling Lab attracts private and public investment; every member of that community is gainfully employed in a fulfilling role. Communities have what they need to solve problems for public and private sectors at the local, national and global levels.
headlines.future: every member gainfully employed in a fulfilling role; communities have what they need to solve problems at every level
headlines.position: every community that hosts a Lab attracts private and public investment

headlines.text: The Upskilling Labs community and workforce model is leading in human agency development; other nations race to adopt it.
headlines.spoken: The Upskilling Labs community and workforce model is leading in human agency development; other nations race to adopt it. We believe in a future of work that's still human-driven, that we've created a system for producing those outcomes, and that others find value in it and use it, at scale, such that we're actually a new institution, whether private or public.
headlines.future: a future of work that is still human-driven
headlines.position: the model leading in human agency development; other nations race to adopt it

headlines.text: A successful Lab in every city, in every country, for everyone, in every industry, in less than 10 years.
headlines.spoken: A successful Lab in every city, in every country, for everyone, in every industry, in less than 10 years. We thought about proliferating beyond what it was originally created for, and making sure it's open access for anyone who wants to learn.
headlines.position: a Lab in every city, in every country, for everyone, in every industry

breakouts.about: Eight How Might We boards, one per tension. Each started from a printed sheet of questions; the team added sticky notes in small breakout groups.

boards.title: Guidance vs. autonomy
prompts: How might we help poderators confidently decide when and how to step in with a Pod that's struggling to get started, without undermining the Pod's chance to self-organize?
How might we simplify/better communicate the transition process from problem definition to teams forming?
How might we provide information/instructions in a central location during a cycle (e.g. website dashboard)?
How might we standardize instructions for a better pod experience, with clearer expectations?
How might we create coherence across goals for participant growth, priorities for sessions, assigned tasks, and messaging?
How might we give ambassadors response frameworks for standard questions and public-facing conversations without eliminating their personal voice?

notes.t: How might we ensure people get to experience all roles on a team?
What structures would help pods organize?
Who is the profile of the person who drops? What do we know about their goals? What about those who stay?
How might we help/support Upskillers to feel self-empowered to ask for help when stuck?
HMW activate the feeling of agency + autonomy early in the build cycle to model expectations of volunteers + upskillers
notes.note: A small note in the corner is unclear.

notes.t: HMW reach agreement on the right level of cycle structure to balance “what am I meant to do” with opportunities for emergent?
How might we hold participants/registrants accountable when signing up for workshops / reducing attrition?

boards.title: Designed connection vs. organic momentum
prompts: How might we help Upskillers build stronger relationships earlier in the build cycle?
How might we reduce drop-off during the build cycle?
How might we encourage more use of our 'digital commons' (aka Slack) early on in the build cycle?
How might we design the buddy system so it builds lasting friendships rather than feeling like an assigned chore?
How might we make event discovery feel like a collaborative activity for the whole ambassador network?
How might we examine the build cycle and investigate the optimal length, and align it with the natural energy of a calendar year?

notes.t: How might we simplify Slack usage and centralize a method of communicating on Slack so that information is not lost and not tracked?
How might we build in reqs for engagement for Upskillers so that we help them break the ice about engaging
How might we help participants find a few peers whose shared goals serve to grow engagement and sense of time well spent?

boards.title: Manual, reactive effort vs. standing systems
prompts: How might we codify our workflows so they require less manual effort?
How might we develop AI tools that would also simplify our operations, like a grant identifying agent?
How might we reduce the manual effort of producing a full post cadence for every workshop, so that volunteer time goes toward strategy instead of repetitive drafting?
How might we centralize performance monitoring across LinkedIn, Luma, and the website, so metrics don't rely on manually reading screenshots?
How might we turn ongoing recruitment needs (mentors, volunteers, Upskillers) into a standing content stream, rather than one-off posts written only when a need becomes urgent?

notes.t: How might we operationalize the USL needs?

boards.title: Tailored experience vs. scalable model
prompts: How might we provide a personalized map/guide for upskillers that helps them achieve their AI learning goals?
How might we increase the variety of workshops we offer for learners at different skill levels and interests?
How might we develop and improve processes and guidelines for OLOS so that we are able to open up development to a larger group?
How might we build a comms playbook and brand toolkit that a new city launching its own Lab could pick up and run with little or no onboarding?

notes.t: How might we attract new upskillers for other sectors so that there is more impact and reach?
How might we build Autonomous pathway for upskillers to immediately see the value they get + be willing to lean in.
notes.note: Marked “Exp vs Scale” in the corner.

notes.t: How might we create a platform that guides users + organizers?
How might we decide what every Lab must keep vs what a new city can change for growth
How might we develop new curricula for workshops tailored to the current build theme?
HMW build a tool that enables participants to design their own learning journey built around our program offers?

boards.title: Cohorts end vs. the community continues
prompts: How might we turn build-cycle graduates into the next cycle's mentors and moderators, rather than starting mentor recruitment from scratch (i.e., your personal network)?
How might we keep track of previous cycle builders?
How might we create an intuitive structured pathway for people to move from participant → practitioner → contributor → leader, such that every cycle/cohort makes the org/next cycle stronger?
How might we transform the people who develop capabilities through The Labs into the people who help develop capabilities in others?

notes.t: HMW create a durable progression from participant to practitioner to contributor to leader, so that each cohort's learning, relationships, and expertise strengthens the next?
How might we keep promising prototypes alive after showcase?
How might we have a colloquium post-presentation retrospective, where we provide portfolioing help in exchange for data/feedback so that both [the end is unclear]
notes.note: The last line is hard to read.

notes.t: HMW scale personal connection between volunteers + Upskillers while the Upskillers are in the build cycle so we can 10x skills transfer
notes.note: “10x skills transfer” is our best reading.

notes.t: HMW build in build cycle interactions that bring visibility to the volunteer opportunities so Upskillers see a path toward mentor[ship]
notes.note: The last word runs off the note.

notes.t: Principle: Participation becomes durable when people can see where they belong next + how their contribution changes the system; otherwise cohort completion becomes natural exit point vs. deeper relationship
How might we design an extended experience journey to deliver value beyond the cycle?
How might we help participants get a balance of contributing strengths + trying new skills? What structures w/i build cycle help that?

boards.short: Volunteer goodwill vs. what we ask of it
boards.title: Volunteer goodwill vs. what we ask of it
prompts: How might we recruit and retain enough volunteer mentors/moderators for each cycle without burning out your existing network of former colleagues?

How might we keep track of mentors and volunteers who actually want to be part of the organization in a volunteer capacity, without burning them out with asks and having them fill out forms that might not get seen?
How might we keep mentors engaged via more than just workshops?
How might we leverage the expertise of our mentors better to help upskillers during the cycle?
How might we improve onboarding/training so that volunteers feel prepared and ready to support a workshop virtually/in-person?
How might we make contribution to The Labs feel like a meaningful form of professional growth, rather than simply another volunteer obligation?
How might we create a contributor culture where delivering hands-on improvements to the system is a core part of participating in the system?

notes.t: HMW build a scalable contributor ecosystem that attracts, prepares, activates, develops, and retains mentors and moderators while making their contributions visibly valuable for Upskillers, The Labs, and their own professional growth?
How do we grow our volunteer network? Where do we source them?
How do we clarify + communicate types of volunteer needs?
Operating principle: Every contribution should have a clear ask, bounded commitment, visible impact, and meaningful return.
How might we let volunteers step back for a cycle without losing touch + saying goodbye?
How can we get AI experts from Frontier Labs join as mentors?
HMW design tiered volunteer roles to make clear how volunteers can scale up their engagement?

boards.title: What we do vs. what we can prove
prompts: How might we ensure we are getting consistent measurement on our outcomes so that we can build a stronger program AND tell our story to partners and funders?
How might we measure the impact of learning opportunities (virtual/in-person workshops, pod experience)?
How might we capture feedback to inform better learning?
How might we clearly articulate metrics of success: is it participant growth, project delivery, or participant and volunteer network numbers?
How might we make the Labs itself better at learning from its own experiments?
How might we strengthen our articulation of who the Labs are for, and the unmet need it addresses for them? (And how do we know this?)
How might we build a funding narrative (grants, sponsors) that reflects impact in terms funders care about, not just activity (workshops held, events run)?

How might we package brand-visible content (recaps, testimonials, metrics) into reusable assets that fundraising and partnership teams can pull from directly, rather than starting from scratch each time?

notes.t: HMW develop longitudinal data gathering to truly measure Upskilling Labs outcomes?
How do we measure confidence?
How might we quantify the impact of our mission?
How might we better measure community impact? jobs, startups,
How might we communicate + deliver on the impact of our mission?
SROI — social return on investment. How might we follow-up w/ Upskillers 6 months → 12 months after a cycle so that we know whether their skills led to new roles/projects/work?
How might we make our mission deliver impact

boards.title: Grant dependence vs. diversified revenue
prompts: How might we start building out other funding streams so that we are relying less on grants?
How might we create income streams for the Labs that are not dependent on donors and grants?
How might we turn a one-time learning opportunity into a more sustainable product?

notes.t: How might we turn The Upskilling Labs into a sustainable non-profit business?
How might we develop an earned revenue strategy that stays true to the mission?
How might we turn funding into an ongoing activity rather than just a passive ask?
How might we get revenue streams from top 10 companies in DMV?
HMW connect with prospective targeted sponsors + donors who want to or already support the Labs' work
